appraisal_events.evidence: il montrait un grand empressement envers des gens du monde... des journalistes, qui lui étaient bien inférieurs... il continuait à simuler la déférence envers des écrivains médiocres pour arriver à être prochainement académicien... l'homme à barbiche et à nez en colimaçon avait des ruses de gentleman voleur de fourchettes, pour se rapprocher du fauteuil académique espéré, de telle duchesse qui disposait de plusieurs voix
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes a gap between Bergotte's genuine literary genius, which the man himself does not fully trust, and his vain, calculating pursuit of academic honors through flattery of inferior writers and a vote-holding duchess, likening him to a scheming kleptomaniac.

appraisal_events.evidence: Il avait agi cruellement avec sa femme. Mais, dans une auberge de village... il était resté pour veiller une pauvresse qui avait tenté de se jeter à l'eau... il avait laissé beaucoup d'argent... De sorte qu'il a excité autour de lui des rancunes justifiées et des gratitudes ineffaçables.
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage closes by holding documented cruelty toward his wife alongside unusual generosity toward a suffering stranger, deliberately refusing to resolve Bergotte's moral character into either condemnation or vindication.

status_effects.explanation: Bergotte is locally diminished as the narrator lays bare his vanity and social scheming, framed in openly damning terms (kleptomaniac, fork-stealing gentleman-thief), even though this is only one alternating facet of him.
The closing anecdotes of cruelty and generosity are held in genuine tension, so the passage yields no net movement, only an explicit, narrator-endorsed ambivalence about his character.

ambiguities: The narrator explicitly states that secondhand testimony (from intimates and strangers) could not settle whether Bergotte was fundamentally good or cruel, so the closing mixed portrait is presented as genuinely irresolvable rather than a hidden verdict.
